approval_timeline.simple: Same day to 1 business day online/OTC for a straightforward residential water heater replacement

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in OR
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
T&P relief valve discharge piped to floor / drain pan per IPC 504
Garage installation: 18 in elevation OR FVIR-listed unit (IPC 504.6)
Seismic strapping (CA/OR/WA): two straps, upper third + lower third
Combustion air provisions or direct-vent unit — verify per IFGC 304

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed Oregon plumbing contractor pulls the permit — the contractor license number must appear on the application. For gas water heater work, the plumbing contractor is the permit holder; owner-builders should not assume they can pull this trade permit without verifying Oregon rules and Portland BDS acceptance.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Bureau of Development Services (BDS)

common_mistakes: Skipping the plumbing permit because it is a simple like-for-like swap — Portland still requires the permit
Using the wrong T&P discharge setup — the relief line must terminate correctly and cannot dump into a wall or improper drain location
Missing seismic strapping/anchorage in Oregon’s earthquake zone
Reusing venting parts that do not match the new appliance listing or draft requirements
Submitting the permit without verifying the contractor’s Oregon license status and Portland acceptance before starting work

Bring the manufacturer install sheet to the job and follow the exact venting and clearance requirements; inspectors in Portland will check the listing details
